label: Total assets under supervision (AUS)
plain: Everything Goldman manages or advises on for a fee, across asset management and wealth management.
say_it: Goldman reported about $4.1 trillion of assets under supervision at the end of September 2026, which includes wealth management and liquidity assets, so it is wider than the asset management client business I am applying to.
caveat: It is a firm-wide figure. It is not the Client Solutions Group's assets and it includes $1,051bn of liquidity products.

label: AUS growth in nine months
plain: Supervised assets grew by about $491bn in nine months, through inflows, markets and acquisitions.
say_it: Supervised assets rose from about $3.6 trillion to $4.1 trillion in nine months, and part of that came from markets and acquisitions, not only client decisions.
caveat: Growth mixes net inflows, market movement and acquired assets such as the $31bn from Innovator.

label: AWM share of firm net revenues
plain: The Asset & Wealth Management segment produced $16,679m of $58,283m firm net revenues.
say_it: Asset & Wealth Management was about 29% of Goldman's net revenues in 2025; the asset management business on its own was closer to 12%.
caveat: 'About 30%' describes the whole segment including wealth management, not asset management alone and not CSG.

label: Asset management share of firm net revenues
plain: The 'Asset management' business inside AWM earned $6,784m in 2025.
say_it: On Goldman's own segment split, asset management was about $6.8bn of revenue in 2025, under 12% of the firm.
caveat: Includes incentive fees and investment gains, which are not recurring client fees.

label: AWM management and other fees
plain: The recurring fee line of the segment: $4,990m from asset management and $6,548m from wealth management.
say_it: Management and other fees were about $11.5bn in 2025, and that recurring line is what the firm points to when it talks about durable revenue.
caveat: Recurring is not guaranteed: it moves with markets, flows and fee rates.

label: AWM pre-tax margin and target
plain: The segment kept 25 cents of pre-tax profit per dollar of revenue and aims for about 30% within three to five years.
say_it: Goldman has set a public target of roughly a 30% pre-tax margin for Asset & Wealth Management, up from 25% in 2025.
caveat: A segment target. It says nothing about the profitability of any client team.

label: Q3 2026 AWM net revenues
plain: The latest quarter before the cutoff, 14% above the same quarter a year earlier.
say_it: In the third quarter of 2026 the segment's revenue was about $5.1bn, with management and other fees of about $3.6bn.
caveat: One quarter; incentive fees of $587m made it unusually strong.

label: Alternative AUS and 2030 target
plain: Supervised alternative assets, and the public growth target.
say_it: Alternatives were $491bn of supervised assets in September 2026, against a stated target of $750bn by the end of 2030.
caveat: Goldman's marketing figure of 'over $706bn in total alternative assets' uses a wider definition; do not mix the two.

label: EMEA share of AUS
plain: The only regional cut Goldman publishes.
say_it: Goldman discloses about $800bn of supervised assets for EMEA; it does not publish a UK figure or a split by client channel within the region.
caveat: No UK figure, no channel-by-region split, and wealth management is included.

label: Institutional long-term AUS
plain: Long-term assets from institutional clients, the largest of three channels.
say_it: Institutional is the largest long-term channel at about $1.25 trillion.
caveat: Global, all regions; says nothing about the UK institutional team.

label: Third-party distributed long-term AUS
plain: Assets that reach Goldman through other firms' distribution, the filing's name for the third-party wealth channel.
say_it: The third-party distributed channel reached about $714bn, up from $567bn at the end of 2025.
caveat: The jump includes acquired ETF assets. 'Third-party distributed' is the filing term; 'Third Party Wealth' is the team name.

label: Wealth management long-term AUS
plain: Assets of Goldman's own private wealth clients.
say_it: Goldman's own wealth clients hold about $1.1 trillion of long-term assets, which sits in a separate channel from third-party wealth.
caveat: Not covered by the Client Solutions Group.

label: Long-term net inflows, first nine months of 2026
plain: Net new long-term money: third-party distributed $97bn, wealth $88bn, institutional $65bn.
say_it: In the first nine months of 2026 the third-party distributed channel had the largest long-term net inflows, about $97bn.
caveat: Net of outflows; includes acquisition-related inflows.

label: Global OCIO assets under supervision
plain: Assets where Goldman acts as outsourced chief investment officer, worldwide.
say_it: Goldman reported $480bn of OCIO assets globally at the end of March 2026, which is why I would not describe OCIO as a UK-only business.
caveat: Global; a later website figure of $540bn+ is dated 30 June 2026. No UK-only OCIO figure is published.

label: BAE Systems pension schemes mandate
plain: Scheme assets covered by the appointment, described by Goldman as the largest UK OCIO mandate to that date.
say_it: The BAE Systems appointment covered about £23bn of defined benefit assets, followed a competitive tender advised by Redington, and brought the schemes' in-house team into Goldman.
caveat: Scheme assets at announcement, not fee-paying revenue. The fee is not public.

label: Shell pension entities mandate
plain: OCIO and advisory appointment by several Shell pension entities and a captive insurer, including about $15.6bn in the UK.
say_it: The Shell mandate was about $40bn in total, of which roughly $15.6bn was UK, after a tender overseen by Isio in which each fund decided for itself.
caveat: Mixes OCIO and advisory assets; Shell's Dutch fund is not part of it.

label: Verizon and Lockheed Martin appointments
plain: $30bn of defined benefit assets under management plus $40bn of defined contribution assets under advisement.
say_it: The July 2026 US appointments were over $70bn, but $40bn of that was assets under advisement, which is a different thing from assets Goldman manages.
caveat: Under advisement is not under management.

label: UK fiduciary market
plain: Isio's measure of UK defined benefit fiduciary management; the mandate count fell for the first time since 2008.
say_it: The UK fiduciary market is around £241bn, and the number of mandates has started to fall while assets concentrate in a few very large delegations.
caveat: One survey; another tracker gives £272bn for 2026.

label: Share of UK fiduciary assets in OCIO-style mandates
plain: A handful of very large delegations hold over half the assets.
say_it: About half of UK fiduciary assets now sit in a small number of very large OCIO-style mandates, which is the part of the market Goldman has been winning.
caveat: Survey data; definitions of 'OCIO-style' vary.

label: Effective management fee, all AUS
plain: Goldman's average fee across all supervised assets: alternatives 58bp, equity 54bp, fixed income 17bp, liquidity 14bp.
say_it: Goldman's average effective management fee was 31 basis points in 2025, ranging from 14 on liquidity to 58 on alternatives, which shows why product mix matters as much as asset growth.
caveat: Firm-wide blends including wealth management. Not the price of any mandate.

label: Advisory and OCIO alternative accounts
plain: The only place OCIO appears in the filings: lumped with advisory accounts, alternatives only.
say_it: Goldman's filings show advisory and OCIO alternative accounts earning about 17 basis points against 77 on funds and discretionary accounts, so OCIO is a scale business at a low rate.
caveat: Alternatives only and combined with advisory. No standalone OCIO fee is disclosed.

label: Commitments raised but not yet earning fees
plain: A commitment only earns a fee once it is drawn and invested (for funds charging on invested capital).
say_it: Of $438bn of alternatives commitments raised from 2020 to 2025, about $105bn was not yet fee-earning, which is why I separate a commitment from fee-paying assets.
caveat: Depends on each fund's fee base.

label: UK fiduciary fees
plain: Price competition for large fiduciary mandates.
say_it: Fiduciary management fees in the UK have fallen by roughly a quarter in five years, mainly on mandates above £500m.
caveat: Market survey, not Goldman's fees.

label: Institutional fee trend
plain: Industry-wide pressure on institutional fees.
say_it: Industry data suggest institutional fees fall about 3% a year, and over 80% of 2025 revenue growth came from markets, not new money.
caveat: Consultant estimate for the whole industry.

label: DB funding ratio (PPF 7800)
plain: UK defined benefit schemes in aggregate hold more assets than their section 179 liabilities: a £275.4bn surplus.
say_it: UK defined benefit schemes are in aggregate surplus, about 134% funded on the PPF measure, so the live question for trustees is endgame, not deficit repair.
caveat: A PPF-basis measure, lower than buyout cost; individual schemes vary widely.

label: Buy-ins in 2025
plain: A record number of insurance transactions, with lower total premium than 2024.
say_it: 2025 saw a record 370 buy-ins but lower total premium, because growth was almost entirely in deals under £100m.
caveat: Volume by count and by value tell different stories.

label: DC default scale requirement
plain: Master trust and group personal pension defaults must reach £25bn by 2030 or be on track by 2035.
say_it: The Pension Schemes Act requires default arrangements to reach £25bn, which pushes defined contribution providers to consolidate and changes who an asset manager needs to know.
caveat: The requirement cannot start before 1 January 2030.

label: LGPS pools
plain: Local government pension pooling reform reduced the number of pools.
say_it: The LGPS now has six pools, and funds must delegate implementation to them, so the buyer for a manager is increasingly the pool.
caveat: Regulations in force 30 June 2026.

label: Fiduciary tender rule
plain: Trustees must run a competitive tender before a fiduciary manager runs 20% or more of scheme assets.
say_it: UK trustees must tender fiduciary mandates above 20% of assets to at least three providers, which is why relationships get you invited and do not get you appointed.
caveat: Applies to trust-based schemes.

label: Bank Rate
plain: The Bank of England's first increase since August 2023 (8–1 vote); the 10-year gilt yielded about 5.15% that day.
say_it: Bank Rate rose to 4% on 5 November 2026, the first increase since 2023, so any view built on falling rates is out of date.
caveat: Nine days before the cutoff; it can change again.

label: Fed funds target range
plain: Held, with two dissents in favour of a rise.
say_it: The Fed held in October with two members voting to raise, so the direction of rates is contested on both sides of the Atlantic.
caveat: A snapshot.

label: European active ETFs launched in 2025
plain: Goldman's build-out of active UCITS ETFs for the wealth channel; about $90bn of ETF assets globally.
say_it: Goldman launched 13 active ETFs in Europe in 2025, which tells me the wealth channel is being asked to sell a wrapper, not just funds.
caveat: The $90bn is global and includes the Innovator acquisition.

label: Innovator acquisition
plain: An acquired active ETF sponsor.
say_it: The Innovator deal added about $31bn of ETF assets, so some of the growth in third-party distributed assets was bought.
caveat: Acquired assets are not organic inflows.

label: UK model portfolio market
plain: Model portfolio services are a growing route to UK advised clients.
say_it: The UK model portfolio market is reported at around £190bn, which makes the people who build models important gatekeepers.
caveat: Snippet-only source.

label: Liquidity products AUS
plain: Money market and short-term assets in the filings; Goldman's website says Liquidity Solutions oversees more than $1.2tn.
say_it: Liquidity is over a trillion dollars of Goldman's supervised assets, at about 14 basis points, so it is a volume business that can move in a day.
caveat: The website's $1.2tn+ uses a wider definition than the filing line.

label: Q3 2026 liquidity net flows
plain: Liquidity products had net outflows in the same quarter long-term assets took in $97bn.
say_it: In the third quarter of 2026 liquidity products saw net outflows while long-term products had strong inflows, which shows cash balances behave differently from mandates.
caveat: One quarter.

label: Insurance general-account assets
plain: Assets managed for insurers' own balance sheets.
say_it: Goldman manages about $651bn of general-account assets for insurers, and its annual survey of 434 insurance investment heads found 62% planning to raise private asset allocations.
caveat: Global. EMEA and UK insurance assets are not disclosed.

label: NN Investment Partners acquisition
plain: The deal that made the Netherlands a major European location and took European AUS above $600bn.
say_it: The 2022 NN Investment Partners acquisition is why The Hague is a major location and why Dutch is asked for in Benelux roles.
caveat: Figures as at completion.

label: Dutch pension transition
plain: Dutch schemes are moving to a new defined contribution-style system.
say_it: About thirty Dutch funds with €542bn had converted by March 2026, with the rest due by 2028, which changes their hedging and investment needs.
caveat: Transition timetable can slip.

label: Partner Class of 2026
plain: Partners are invited in a named class; it is not an automatic rung after managing director.
say_it: Partner at Goldman is an invitation in a biennial class, 109 people in the latest, so it is not simply the next title up.
caveat: Firm-wide.

label: Multi-asset solutions team behind OCIO
plain: The investing group that runs OCIO portfolios.
say_it: A Goldman executive said the OCIO business is supported by a multi-asset solutions team of more than 300 people.
caveat: A statement by an executive in trade press; global.

label: Application limit
plain: Extra applications are automatically withdrawn.
caveat: A rule about applications, not about chances.

label: Programme length
plain: Summer analyst programme with orientation, training and real responsibilities.
caveat: Programme-wide wording; the London CSG listing has no team-specific duties.

label: Final round
plain: The 'Superday' for campus hires, after a video interview of about 30 minutes.
caveat: General Goldman process. This team's exact format is not published.

label: Analyst base pay (London)
plain: The £52k and £48k figures come only from the former intern.
caveat: Do not quote either figure.
